The long U, in detail

Concept E with your two changes: much more detail on the station, and the building area filling the whole inside of the U. The U is the drydock frame, so a bigger frame means a bigger U. The ship stays nose up inside, which is fine for building.

E

Long U, mouth to the gate

THE SHIPYARD · RIM

Click the building area, a building, the gate or the fleet moorings to fly the camera there.

The walls are plate runs in slightly different tones with a lattice truss on the outside and three conduits (power, data, the mind's violet) along the inside. Window rows glow where the yard is running; gantry cranes with hoist lines and docking clamps reach the ship; work lights pool on the floor; a few drones move around the hull. Red and green lights mark the arm tips and the gate pylons; chevrons lead from the mouth to the gate.

Research (with dishes) and the fabricator sit on the top wall between radiator fins; the test range tower and its target lane hang under the bottom wall next to a dark salvage bay; the mind is joined to the base by violet conduits; fleet moorings run off the left edge on a truss bridge.

In the game

Building area
The drydock grid is exactly the inside of the U. Zooming in on it (D, or a click) is the drydock: the panels slide in, the walls stay around the edges as the frame you build in.
Growth
A bigger frame rebuilds the U around a bigger area; buildings light up their windows when they come online; new buildings (fabricator, salvage bay) appear in their slots; escorts fill the moorings.
Detail budget
All of this is flat vector shapes and a few soft glows, like the ships: a few hundred quads and one or two draw calls, built once and rebuilt only when the yard changes.
